The Financial Planning and Analysis Manager will be responsible for developing insightful analyses that will support timely and effective decision making throughout the organization. You will work closely with senior management and department leads to help develop a long term business plan as well as a detailed annual budget. You will then work to formulate and refine the strategy and financial projections for the business on a quarterly basis. This position requires intense attention to detail and a desire to solve complex business issues.  The key components of the role include:
Budgeting and Forecasting
Collaborate with business leaders to build annual bottoms-up departmental and organizational budgets. Be a resource for resolving issues and provide training and guidance as needed
Develop comprehensive reporting of assumptions, financial statements, and operational metrics derived from the budget process for internal and external stakeholders
Prepare monthly actual to operating budget variances and examine with departmental leaders to determine whether operational changes are required
Lead headcount modeling & track financial impact on headcount changes
Generate cash forecasts with visibility into future liquidity needs
Lead the quarterly re-forecasting process and provide analysis of actual and forecasted variances from original budget
Lead and deliver on Digital Finance transformation by identifying areas for technology adoption and streamlining
Perform ad hoc analysis where required to assist in management decision making
Key Performance Indicators (KPI’s)
Engage with management to identify and track key performance indicators (KPI’s) and bridge analysis to financial performance
Deliver innovative tools to gather data and construct formats for leadership review and discussion
Employ data analysis techniques to identify risks and suggest mitigating strategies
Drive business case preparation and financial return modeling for investment of enterprise resources
Simplify, standardize, and automate analyses for real-time consumption across a broad audience
Financial Reporting
Partner with the People Operations team to ensure that confidential headcount information is reconciled monthly and changes are properly reflected in actual and forecasted financial results
Support the Accounting team in the design, documentation, and maintenance of internal control processes
Assist in the preparation of financial reports for external parties of interest
Assist in the preparation for year-end audits
Performs other duties and special projects as assigned

The Workplace Experience Manager owns the day-to-day experience and operation of Apptronik's Sunnyvale site, an executive- and VIP-heavy location supporting our perception AI and product teams. This person is the face of the workplace and the owner of a site that must be polished, functional, and demo-ready at all times, and personally owns the reception desk as the front-of-house presence for the office. Because Facilities leadership is on-site only periodically, the role operates with a high degree of independence: it anticipates needs, makes sound day-to-day decisions within clear guardrails, and resolves issues before they surface rather than waiting for direction. When executives and VIPs visit, this role ensures the site and executive briefing center are clean, stocked, secure, and physically demo-ready, and delivers a polished front-of-house and guest experience, in support of the executive assistant team, who own meeting logistics, AV, agendas, and the executive's schedule. The role requires the professional poise to work credibly with everyone from vendors and janitorial staff to C-level leadership, and the judgment to respectfully push back when a request to the workplace is unreasonable or unworkable.
Scope & Boundaries
This is a workplace and site-operations role, not an executive assistant role. Executive calendars, travel, meeting logistics, AV, expense reporting, and executive/staff offsites are owned by the EA team. This role owns the physical site, the reception desk and front-of-house experience, the guest and workplace experience, vendors, and site readiness. The two are deliberately complementary: the EA runs the executive's day; the Workplace Experience Manager runs the site the executive walks into. This role sits on its own growth path within Workplace & Facilities and is not a stepping-stone into or out of executive support. The role is expected to operate independently within defined guardrails and to follow clear escalation pathways to Facilities leadership for anything structural, financial beyond approved thresholds, safety-related, or outside its lane.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Own and manage the reception desk as the site's front-of-house post, personally staffing it and/or coordinating coverage, greeting and directing employees, guests, vendors, and VIPs, and setting the standard for every arrival.
Own the daily experience and operation of the Sunnyvale site, ensuring it is consistently polished, functional, and ready for employees, executives, and VIP guests.
Act as the face of the workplace and the site’s decision-maker for day-to-day operations, exercising independent judgment between Facilities leadership visits and escalating what genuinely warrants it through defined pathways.
Keep the site and executive briefing center presentation- and demo-ready at all times, clean, stocked, functional, secure, so the space is never a variable when VIPs arrive.
During VIP visits and executive meetings, provide front-of-house, guest, facility, and vendor support to the EA and executive teams (who own logistics, AV, and agenda).
Own visitor management (e.g., Envoy/VMS), check-in, and badging, and keep the reception area welcoming and well-organized so every guest, from vendors to VIPs, has a smooth, secure, professional arrival.
Identify, build, and manage local vendor relationships including catering as needed (janitorial supplies, beverage, etc.), managing performance to a high standard day-to-day.
Maintain supply, pantry, and workspace readiness so the site never scrambles ahead of a visit or event.
Partner with HR and Recruiting on onboarding logistics, workspace setup, access coordination, and first-day readiness.
Plan and lead site-wide, all-employee workplace and culture events (the EA team owns executive and staff offsites).
Own seating and workspace planning as the site scales toward ~80 employees by the end of 2026.
Proactively surface facility, safety, and vendor risks; hold the space and its vendors to a demo-ready standard.
Maintain discretion and sound judgment around executives, guests, and confidential or VIP activity.
fields.requirements:
Proactive, ownership mindset, a genuine go-getter who runs a site independently and anticipates needs rather than reacting to them.
Clear understanding of boundaries and escalation: knows what to own, what to route to Facilities, and what belongs to other teams (EA, HR).
Hospitality-forward and comfortable personally staffing a reception desk as the front-of-house presence of the office.
Professional poise and a genuine backbone: credible with all levels, from vendors to C-suite, with the judgment to push back diplomatically.
High-energy community builder who sets a site’s tone and culture.
Strong vendor coordination and day-to-day management skills.
Familiarity with visitor management (e.g., Envoy) and ticketing (e.g., Jira), or comparable systems.
Excellent communication, discretion, and interpersonal judgment.
Collaborative partner to the EA and HR teams, with clear respect for role boundaries and no interest in owning executive-support work.
Comfort operating in a fast-paced, ambiguous, early-stage site environment.
Education and/or Experience
High school diploma or equivalent required.
Associate/Bachelor’s or coursework in business administration, hospitality, or workplace management preferred.
3–5 years in reception, hospitality, guest services, workplace experience, office administration, or facilities coordination, ideally including a guest- or executive-facing environment. This is not an entry-level role, the emphasis is on a proven ability to operate independently and take ownership, not on tenure.
Physical Requirements
Ability to move throughout the office during the workday.
Ability to sit at and staff the reception desk for extended periods.
Ability to lift and move office supplies up to 25 lbs as needed (physicality is minimal, e.g., refilling a printer).
Ability to work at a desk and use computer systems for coordination tasks.
Vision and hearing sufficient to communicate effectively with employees and visitors.
Work Location
On-Site Only, M–F, 100% on-site, no remote flexibility.
Occasional overtime for events or emergencies.

Our flagship humanoid robot, Apollo, is built to collaborate thoughtfully with people, starting with critical industries such as manufacturing and logistics, with future applications in healthcare, the home, and beyond.
We operate at the cutting edge of Applied AI, applying our expertise across the full robotics stack to solve some of society's most important problems. You will join a team dedicated to bringing Apollo to market at scale, tackling the complex challenges like safety, commercialization, and mass production to change the world for the better.
Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced Technical Accounting & Financial Reporting Senior Manager to join our team as the first member of our technical accounting function. This position will support us as we work to build and deploy some of the coolest robots on Earth.
Reporting directly to the Controller, you will serve as the Company's technical accounting and financial reporting leader, acting as the primary resource for complex accounting matters and the accounting implications of new business initiatives. You will partner closely with Finance, FP&A, Legal, Operations, Engineering, executive leadership, external auditors, and outside consultants to support the Company's continued growth and IPO-readiness journey.
As the first dedicated technical accounting hire, you will establish and maintain the Company's accounting policy framework, prepare technical accounting analyses, support financial reporting and audit activities, drive public-company readiness initiatives, and build the technical accounting function from the ground up, with the opportunity to grow and lead that function through the IPO and beyond as the Company scales.
Key Responsibilities
Serve as the Company's subject matter expert on U.S. GAAP and lead the research, interpretation, and application of complex accounting standards to current and future company activities, including:
Revenue recognition, including hardware, software, and service arrangements
Manufacturing and inventory-related accounting matters
Capitalized software costs and research and development activities
Stock-based compensation
Equity and financing transactions, including convertible instruments
Lessee and lessor arrangements
International operations
Business combinations and strategic transactions
Lead the preparation of high-quality technical accounting memos, accounting policies, and financial statement disclosures, ensuring compliance with U.S. GAAP and supporting the Company's evolving business model and growth initiatives.
Own the technical accounting and financial reporting aspects of the Company's audit, IPO readiness, and public-company preparation efforts, including support for external audits, disclosure processes, internal controls, and future SEC reporting requirements.
Partner closely with Finance, FP&A, Legal, Operations, Engineering, and executive leadership to evaluate new products, customer arrangements, strategic partnerships, financing activities, and other significant transactions, providing practical accounting guidance during business decision-making.
Act as the primary liaison with external auditors and third-party specialists, including valuation, tax, and consulting advisors, to support technical accounting conclusions and regulatory compliance.
Support the monthly and quarterly close processes for technical accounting matters and help develop scalable processes, policies, and controls to support a rapidly growing organization.
Assist the CFO and Controller with special projects, Board and management presentations, strategic initiatives, and other financial reporting and accounting matters as needed.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance
CPA designation required, with current knowledge of U.S. GAAP principles and their practical application
7+ years of progressive accounting experience, including at least 3-4 years in a Big 4 or national public accounting firm and meaningful technical accounting/financial reporting experience in industry, operating at the Manager or Senior Manager level
Hands-on experience with revenue recognition, stock-based compensation, equity and financing transactions, and software capitalization
Demonstrated proficiency in researching and applying complex accounting guidance
Strong written communication skills, including drafting technical accounting memoranda and financial statement disclosures
Ability to communicate complex financial concepts clearly to both financial and non-financial stakeholders and management
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in high-growth technology, robotics, manufacturing, AI, hardware, and/or R&D-intensive environments, including exposure to inventory, capitalized manufacturing costs, and other hardware-related accounting matters
Experience supporting companies through IPO readiness, SEC reporting, public-company preparation, or other significant capital markets transactions
Experience with lessor accounting or hardware-as-a-service / usage-based commercial models
Attributes
A high degree of initiative, ownership, and self-reliance, appropriate to being the first member of the technical accounting team
A practical and collaborative mindset, suited to a highly fluid environment
Comfort operating in an entrepreneurial environment with evolving processes, limited infrastructure, and significant cross-functional collaboration
Ability to build scalable processes and frameworks from the ground up
*This is a direct hire.  Please, no outside Agency solicitations.

We are seeking an experienced Corporate Tax Manager to join our team as the first member of our tax function. This position will support us as we work to build and deploy some of the coolest robots on Earth.
As the first dedicated corporate tax hire, you will have the unique opportunity to build and lead the tax function from the ground up. You will establish and maintain the company’s tax policies, processes, and governance, with the opportunity to grow the function as the Company scales. You will collaborate internally with the accounting team to ensure accurate tax accounting and serve as the central point of contact with external auditors on tax matters.
Reporting directly to the Controller, you will partner closely with external advisors to ensure direct tax compliance at the federal and state level, support tax planning initiatives, and coordinate data gathering for R&D tax credit studies.
Additionally, you will oversee our indirect tax processes, including coordinating with external advisors on property tax renditions, sales and use tax compliance, and the administration of the company’s indirect tax software.
Key Responsibilities
Manage and review work performed by third-party providers regarding federal and state income tax compliance including filings, extensions, and payments
Oversee indirect taxes, including sales/use and property taxes, and eventually international VAT matters.
Manage income tax accounting and reporting under ASC 740, including tax provision preparation, deferred tax calculations and reconciliations, and related disclosures.
Work with external advisors to support the development and implementation of tax strategies & planning opportunities
Identify and develop processes to increase efficiency, including data gathering for R&D tax credit reviews and general accounting process improvements
Build and maintain effective internal controls over tax accounting and reporting
Support the CFO and Controller on ad hoc projects, education for internal stakeholders, and presentations to management
Participate in month-end close activities for tax-related accounting matters
Act as liaison with external auditors

Knowledge of sales and use regulations and compliance; experience using Avatax software preferred

Experience in managing relationships with external providers of tax services

fields.duties:
We are seeking a highly experienced, versatile, and execution-oriented Technical Sourcer to lead sourcing strategy and execution for our fast-paced hiring needs across software, hardware, and product teams.
In this role, you will not be restricted to a single technical specialty; instead, you will apply deep sourcing expertise across multiple disciplines, shaping sourcing standards and pipeline strategy for our Mountain View, CA office. Additionally, as the senior recruiting team member and sole recruiting presence in our Mountain View location, you will serve as the trusted advisor and operational leader for local hiring—partnering with local site leadership and cross-functional interviewing teams to design, coordinate, and continuously improve all CA office-specific on-site interview loops.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES or KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES
Partner with recruiters, hiring managers, and site leadership to shape sourcing strategy across diverse engineering domains, including Hardware (ME, EE, Embedded), Software, and Product roles, translating ambiguous hiring needs into scalable sourcing plans.
Lead the sourcing of qualified passive candidates using various channels, including LinkedIn Recruiter, GitHub, technical publications, and active networking within deep tech, software, and hardware communities, continually refining channel strategy and sharing best practices that raise sourcing effectiveness across the team.
Screen resumes and conduct initial vetting calls, exercising sound judgment to assess technical baseline capability, alignment with role scope, and cultural add, while coaching others on effective screening practices.
Serve as the primary on-site Talent Acquisition representative and trusted advisor for the Mountain View office. Partner with local site leadership and cross-functional interviewing teams to design, coordinate, host, and continuously improve all CA-specific on-site interview loops, ensuring a seamless, high-touch experience.
Own candidate pipeline management and applicant tracking system (Greenhouse) data integrity, identifying and resolving process gaps that affect data quality or compliance.
Analyze pipeline and sourcing data to evaluate program effectiveness, delivering data-driven insights and recommendations to hiring managers and the broader People team on talent market conditions across software, hardware, and product landscapes.
fields.requirements:
Deep expertise in technical sourcing, with a proven ability to fluently pivot between software, hardware, and product management domains and apply sound judgment to ambiguous or complex sourcing challenges.
Track record of designing and scaling creative sourcing strategies that unearth niche talent beyond standard job postings, and sharing techniques that raise sourcing standards across the team.
Demonstrated ability to build trusted, influential partnerships with local Mountain View site leadership, diverse interview teams, and candidates alike, shaping how the function engages with the site.
Outstanding organizational skills with a proven ability to independently manage real-time interview logistics, scheduling variables, and physical on-site hosting, while improving processes for scalability.
Comfortable operating as the senior recruiting presence in a satellite office; self-motivated, proactive, and resilient through changing business and engineering priorities, exercising independent judgment with minimal oversight.
High proficiency with modern applicant tracking systems (e.g., Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby) and sourcing discovery tools, with the ability to identify and address data quality or reporting gaps.
Embodies the company values of Curiosity, Humility, Integrity, Passion, and Creativity (CHIPC).
EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE
8+ years of technical sourcing or full-cycle recruiting experience in a fast-paced startup or high-growth technology environment, with demonstrated impact at a senior or staff level.
Demonstrated track record of leading talent-mapping and pipeline-building strategy across a mixed portfolio of hardware, software, and product roles, and influencing sourcing standards beyond a single team.
Prior experience serving as a trusted advisor to local office stakeholders and independently leading end-to-end interview coordination loops.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS
Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times
Vision to read printed materials and a computer screen
Hearing and speech to communicate clearly with on-site candidates and internal teams
The annual salary range for this role is $165,000-$235,000.
*This is a direct hire.  Please, no outside Agency solicitations.

We are seeking a strategic and experienced Senior Staff HR Business Partner to support our corporate functions, including Sales, Strategy, Customer Experience, Marketing, Information Technology, Finance, and Legal. In this role, you will serve as a trusted advisor to leaders and managers, helping drive organizational effectiveness, talent strategies, workforce planning, leadership capability, and employee engagement. You will partner closely with business leaders to align people strategies with business objectives while supporting a high-performing, rapidly evolving organization.
This is an exciting opportunity for an HR professional who enjoys balancing strategic consulting with hands-on execution and thrives in a dynamic, growth-oriented environment.
What You'll Do
Partner with senior leaders to develop and execute people strategies that support business objectives and organizational growth.
Act as a trusted advisor on organizational effectiveness, team design, leadership effectiveness, and talent-related business challenges.
Support organizational changes, including restructures, leadership transitions, and growth initiatives, ensuring thoughtful change management and communication strategies.
Drive talent review, succession planning, and leadership development efforts.
Coach managers and leaders on performance management, employee development, team effectiveness, and leadership best practices.
Support initiatives that strengthen employee engagement, retention, and career growth.
Advise leaders on complex employee relations matters, including performance management, conduct concerns, workplace issues, and conflict resolution.
Lead investigations and case management activities, exercising sound judgment and maintaining confidentiality.
Ensure consistent application of employment laws, company policies, and People Operations practices.
Partner with leaders to proactively identify and mitigate organizational and people-related risks.
Provide actionable recommendations to leaders based on talent, engagement, turnover, organizational health, and workforce planning data.
Partner closely with Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, Learning & Development, and other HR Centers of Excellence to deliver integrated people solutions.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of HR programs, policies, and processes.
Help shape and enhance scalable people practices that support organizational growth.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field.
8+ years of progressive HR experience, including significant experience as an HR Business Partner supporting business leaders.
Experience supporting corporate and/or customer-facing functions such as Sales, Marketing, Finance, IT, Professional Services, Customer Success, or Service.
Strong employee relations expertise, including conducting investigations and resolving complex workplace issues.
Experience advising leaders on organizational design, change management, workforce planning, and talent management.
Strong business acumen and ability to connect people strategies to business outcomes.
Excellent consulting, coaching, influencing, and stakeholder management skills.
Experience using people analytics and workforce data to drive decisions.
Preferred Qualifications
Master's degree in Human Resources, Business, Organizational Development, or a related field.
HR certification such as SHRM-SCP, SPHR, or equivalent.
Experience supporting global teams and distributed workforces.
Experience with sales compensation structures, including variable pay programs, commission plans, and incentive design principles in partnership with Finance, Sales, and Compensation teams
Experience in high-growth technology, robotics, engineering, software, or customer-facing service organizations.
We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas for this position.
The base pay range for this position is between $138,000 to $168,000 annually. Base pay will depend on multiple individualized factors including, but not limited to internal equity, job related knowledge, skills and experience. This range represents a good faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting. Boston Dynamics offers a generous Benefits package including medical, dental vision, 401(k), paid time off and a annual bonus structure. Additional details regarding these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer for employment.

Boston Dynamics is seeking a highly organized Technical Trainer to design, deliver, and manage training and documentation for the Atlas Data Operations (ADOPS) team and external product operators. This role requires experience creating content and delivering technical subject matter to both technical and non-technical audiences, a passion for learning new technologies quickly, and the ability to build strong relationships with a world-class engineering team to stay current on product enhancements.
The Atlas Data Operations team consists of robot pilots who teleoperate robots and produce data to train Atlas, which is focused on advancing machine learning and manipulation capabilities. Your ideas will change what robots can do!
Schedule/Working Hours
Monday - Friday: 40 hours per week, regular hours (e.g., 9 AM to 6 PM).
Periodic flexibility is required to cover first and second shift or provide off-hours support to maintain continuous operations.
Core Responsibilities
Training Design & Delivery
Design, maintain, and continuously improve the ADOPS Pilot Onboarding and Levelling Process. Training includes hardware, software, and process content.
Lead and administer interactive, instructor-led training for ADOPS Robot Pilots. Occasionally the Technical Trainer will provide training to other parties including partner organizations and external product operators.
Deliver training on commercially available BD product-lines, software, APIs, and solution infrastructures.
Coach and assess ADOPS Robot Pilots, providing feedback on best practices to improve techniques.
Perform periodic pilot skills assessments to determine systemic gaps or regressions, collect feedback to track knowledge retention, and inform continuous improvement efforts for all training programs.
Documentation & Process Management
Act as a Data Ops process specialist, owning the document change control process for all Data Operations documentation.
Develop and maintain high-standard technical training content, including task playbooks, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), presentations, and hands-on exercises.
Codify best techniques and practices from veteran pilots and engineers, translating them into required documentation and training materials.
Facilitate clear communication channels between Data Ops, Engineering, CL&D, and other partner teams to align on documentation, project status, and operational needs.
Required Skills & Experience
Bachelor’s degree preferred, or equivalent professional experience in formalized instructional systems, curriculum management, or technical training leadership (including military equivalents). High School diploma or GED required.
Proven experience as a technical trainer, documentation specialist, or teacher, with demonstrated success communicating complex technical subject matter to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience prompting generative AI to create and optimize polished documents from source content
Demonstrated ability to curate and develop curriculum for supporting Instructor-Led Training programs.
Self-directed with proven experience managing small projects or operations in a fast-paced R&D, lab, or technology-focused environment.
Strong computer proficiency; familiarity with robotics concepts, VR systems, or machine learning data pipelines is highly desirable.
Comfortable wearing and operating VR headsets, motion capture suits, and handheld VR controllers for extended sessions.
Note: VR use can be physically demanding and may cause discomfort or motion sickness for some individuals.
Practical hands-on experience with mechanical or electrical systems, enterprise network environments, or familiarity with Linux command line interface/Python is a plus.
Key Attributes
Exceptional organizational skills, clear attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with confidence engaging with customers, stakeholders, and team members in a collaborative setting.
Proactive, self-directed problem-solver who can investigate issues and consult documentation before escalating.
Ability to thrive in ambiguous, dynamic, and rapidly evolving technical environments.
Reliable, punctual, and committed to structured process and accurate documentation.
The pay range for this position is between $73,000 to $101,000 annually. Base pay will depend on multiple individualized factors including, but not limited to internal equity, job related knowledge, skills and experience. This range represents a good faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting. Boston Dynamics offers a generous Benefits package including medical, dental vision, 401(k), paid time off and a annual bonus structure. Additional details regarding these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer for employment.

As a Senior Treasury Specialist, you will be a key contributor within the Treasury
Department, responsible for the efficient management of the firm's liquidity position, funding and debt management, interest rate/credit risk hedging, and investment portfolio. The Senior Treasury Specialist is responsible for treasury accounting, its impact on accurate financial records, and building cross-functional stakeholder relationships.
The incumbent leverages strong, detail-oriented analytical and problem-solving skills to monitor, measure, and manage Boston Dynamics’s liquidity risk, and must have the ability to recognize and understand the cross functional impact of transactions. To thrive in this role, you must have strong communication skills, proficiency in Excel, the ability to prioritize tasks, to work on multiple engagements and manage rapidly changing assignments, and to work independently and in groups.
Boston Dynamics is a world leader in mobile robots, tackling some of the toughest robotics challenges. For years, our awe-inspiring viral videos on YouTube have shown the world what remarkably capable robots can do. Now we are quickly becoming a recognized leader in automation solutions for industrial applications and warehouse logistics.
Key Responsibilities:
 Provide daily oversight, guidance, and technical expertise on the company’s
liquidity position.
 Produce and present comprehensive liquidity risk reports, metrics, and
dashboards for senior management, risk committees, and regulatory bodies.
 Contribute to the development and implementation of funding and liquidity risk management strategies, ensuring alignment with both internal risk guidelines and external regulatory requirements.
 Develop, measure, and refine liquidity risk models and stress-testing frameworks to project cash flows, funding requirements, and buffer adequacy under various economic scenarios.
 Manage a high-quality, low-risk asset portfolio to ensure optimal liquidity buffers, and monitor intraday liquidity to guarantee the firm meets its payment and
settlement obligations efficiently.
 Participate in the monthly close process by maintaining assigned accounts in
compliance with IFRS and US GAAP principles and organizational policies and
within established schedules.
 Participate in projects aimed at enhancing the firm's liquidity management systems, including the implementation of Firm Banking (Host-to-Host)
integrations and establishing SOX 404 compliant internal controls over cash
disbursements.
 Other duties, as assigned.
Qualifications:
 Bachelor’s Degree in Finance or Accounting, Master’s degree preferred
 3 – 5 years of progressive Treasury-related experience, experience at a public
company, with firm banking, hedging FX risk, and managing an investment
portfolio preferred
 Proficiency in accounting software and ERP systems
 Strong interpersonal skills including written and verbal communication,
collaboration, and problem solving
 Strong analytical, organizational and time-management skills
 Demonstrated ability to work independently and as part of a team
 Professional designations such as CFA, FRM, or CTP are highly desirable
We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas for this position.
This position will be on-site at our Waltham location.
Boston Dynamics will never ask you to divulge your personal financial or account information as part of its recruiting process.
The pay range for this position is between $102,000 to $135,000 annually. Base pay will depend on multiple individualized factors including, but not limited to internal equity, job related knowledge, skills and experience. This range represents a good faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting. Boston Dynamics offers a generous Benefits package including medical, dental vision, 401(k), paid time off and a annual bonus structure. Additional details regarding these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer for employment.
